short: A continuously updated agent benchmark spanning coding, finance, biology, and hardware design — with the best agents near 34%.
definition: Frontier-Bench is an AI-agent benchmark built by the team behind Terminal-Bench and the Harbor framework, designed to keep pace with rapidly improving models rather than being replaced. Its first version contains 74 difficult, hands-on tasks that reach beyond coding into fields like finance, music, biology, and hardware design, each run in a real computer environment. It is a community effort with a live, evolving leaderboard, and the tasks are hard enough that the best agents currently solve only about a third of them. It succeeds Terminal-Bench as a moving-target measure of frontier agent ability.
